subject: lavaan.shiny - Feedback and Feature Requests Appreciated

messages.author: 3118bda730f2c124
messages.subject: lavaan.shiny - Feedback and Feature Requests Appreciated
parts:
lavaan.shiny is an R package which connects the lavaan package to a Shiny interface. It's meant to be used as a teaching tool for people who are new to R. I was hoping that people could try it out and give me some feedback on what they like and dislike about it, things that can be improved or changed, and features that people would find helpful.


Currently you can get lavaan.shiny though

CRAN: http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/lavaan.shiny/index.html

GitHub (Development Release): https://github.com/kylehamilton/lavaan.shiny/

Online Demo: http://kylehamilton.net/shiny/lavaan.shiny/


Thanks in advance!

Kyle

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: lavaan.shiny - Feedback and Feature Requests Appreciated
parts:
I like the fact that you can easily paste some data from a space/tab-delimited text file or Excel spreadsheet.  The fact that all variables are automatically displayed in the descriptives is a little distracting.  Perhaps add a checklist of available variables to summarize.  In fact, you could have 1 section for continuous and one for categorical, with options for 1- or 2-way tables?  If you want a simpler function for displaying all variables appropriately, the rockchalk package has a summarize() function that is pretty good at automatically detecting numeric variables with few categories and treating them as continuous.

For fitting the model, perhaps add some TRUE/FALSE lavaan() options as checkboxes and other options as drop-down menus or radio buttons, along with the estimator and SE options you put on a separate tab.  Likewise, provide some options for the summary() output (e.g., rsquare, modindices, nd) along with the defaults you provided (fit = TRUE, stand = TRUE).  You can see the arguments on the lavaan-class help page

help("lavaan-class", lavaan)

I was working on a similar demonstration last year for fitting a model to multiple-population-level data.  It is unfinished, but has some code for implementing a few of these ideas, if you're interested.  I attached it -- feel free to borrow any syntax in there.

Terry

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: lavaan.shiny - Feedback and Feature Requests Appreciated
parts:
It looks really interesting. 

Some observations and recommendations, 
  • the diagram doesnt show complete for me
  • in the estimator options I dont see: MLR, MLM, MML, and others
  • since bootstrap is available it would be useful to use not just for the standard errors but to show the confidence intervals too, with the parameterestimates() function
  • when including ordered variables is not clear how do you tell it to treat them as such
  • the correlation and scatterplot should be able to select which variables to include, with even small data sets these would be impossible to read
  • it need some way to use the arguments of the lavaan functions like std.lv, etc
  • it would be good if you can include the use of other functions like fitMeasures() and functions from semTools like moreFitIndices() and others. There are functions like these that are important to show a variety of ways to evaluate fit instead of just using CFI, TLI, RMSEA and SRMR. For teaching I consider relevant to see the wide variety of fit indices
glad to see projects like this

parts:
Hi,

One thing that you could add is displaying the residuals and possibly use some kind of heat map type presentation to indicate which parts of the residual covariance matrix contains large residuals. Also the kernel density plot of standardized residuals to show that they are about  normal and mostly between -.1 and .1 would be useful.

plot(density(residuals(MeasurementModelResults)$cov))

Mikko
